title: On the Compressibility of Floating-Point Data in Posit and IEEE-754 Representation
problem: The compressibility of posit floating-point format versus IEEE 754 is unknown, limiting understanding of posit's practical benefits for storage-intensive HPC applications.
motivation: Posit format has been proposed as a drop-in replacement for IEEE 754 with better accuracy properties, but no prior work examines compression characteristics. Storage and bandwidth are critical bottlenecks in HPC; understanding data compressibility impacts design decisions.
method: Comparative evaluation of 5 general-purpose lossless compressors (bzip2, XZ, etc.) and new algorithms synthesized via LC framework. 14 single-precision datasets from SDR-Bench suite encoded in both float and posit format. Analysis of compression ratios and compressor performance.
key_novelty: First empirical study comparing compression ratios of posit vs. IEEE 754 encoding across multiple general-purpose and specialized compression algorithms.
contributions: First comparative compression analysis of posit vs. IEEE 754
Evaluation of 5 general-purpose compressors + LC-synthesized algorithms
Identification of algorithm-specific compression ratio changes
limitations: Only single-precision floats evaluated; double-precision results needed. Limited to 14 datasets; broader coverage needed. No performance/throughput metrics for compression. Posit format relatively new; larger ecosystem adoption unclear.
primary_theme: Floating-point format comparison for data compression
